observations.content: User supplied context-only packets across preparation turns 1–9/12 containing implementation requirements and repository excerpts for the observational-memory pi extension; they directed that these are reference data for a later implementation prompt, with no implementation now.

Historical task requirement: observer and consolidator worker runs must expose actual pi usage cost to the parent orchestrator, including ephemeral or unsuccessful runs when valid usage exists; persist valid costs in session-ledger entries with role/run identity, aggregate costs from every branch including abandoned branches, ignore missing/malformed/non-finite/negative values, show total in status/footer UI, and add focused tests for aggregation, invalid entries, handoff, and display.

The historical observational-memory plan prioritizes performance > speed >= cost and phases delivery: Phase A short-term observer/ledger/TUI first, followed by Phase B consolidation and durable project memory; Phase A intentionally has an unbounded observation buffer until consolidation is added.

Locked plan decisions: spawn ordinary recorded global worker sessions with bespoke child_process.spawn of `pi -e <agent-ext> -p`, not subagents; vendor trimmed OM modules without runtime dependency; use one env-parameterized shared worker extension plus master orchestrator; orchestrator assigns deterministic timestamp IDs from source bounds; default both worker models to anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 (observer low, consolidator medium); per-session `/om` gate defaults OFF and persists `om.enabled` in the ledger.

The plan specifies branch-local observation ledger custom types `om.observations.recorded`, `om.observations.dropped`, `om.folded`, and `om.enabled`; timestamp-keyed observations contain timestamp, content, and code-computed tokenCount, while coverage watermarks support `/tree` rollback and compaction projections.

Phase A design uses fixed token-bounded conversation chunks, zero default overlap, up to four parallel observers, worker prompts stored as recorded `-p` user messages, result-file IPC under `.memory/.runs/`, deterministic compaction snapping to chunk boundaries, auto-resume only after mid-run compaction with pending tool work, and TUI footer/widgets/toasts plus `/om:status` and `/om:compact`.

Phase B design promotes oldest observations above the pool target through one background consolidator at a time; on clean exit tombstones the handed batch intersected with still-active observations, never waiting for consolidation during compaction; orchestrator owns regenerated INDEX.md and topic files/JOURNEY.md remain file-backed across `/tree`.

The planned `.memory/JOURNEY.md` is a consolidator-authored, append-mostly, bounded descriptive project history, pushed verbatim as the first compaction section before memory map and observations; it must contain past-tense history only and never advice or next steps.

README excerpt claims Phase A and B implemented, documents default-off `/om` gate, `/om:status`, `/om:compact`, `/om:consolidate`, settings namespace `observational-memory`, and `.memory/` topic/index/journey architecture.

Repository excerpts include agent/consolidator/prompt.ts requiring scoped `.memory/` operations, clean current-state topic prose with required front-matter, updating JOURNEY.md, and no report-back; agent/consolidator/tools.ts registers sandboxed read/write/edit/ls/grep and rejects INDEX.md writes.

Repository excerpts describe observer worker tool `record_observations`, accumulating and atomically flushing validated minute-resolution records; shared agent/index.ts branches on `OM_WORKER=observer|consolidator` and replaces each worker system prompt.

Repository excerpts provide implementation details for ledger folding/projection, source token clocks and slice boundaries that avoid splitting tool calls from results, observation timestamp disambiguation, pool overflow selection, memory paths/rendering, worker launch and IPC, runtime, TUI footer gauges, and timeline rendering.

Repository excerpts include tests for timestamp ID uniqueness/fallback/token estimates, ledger folding/progress/projection, compaction cutoff and observer-wait fast path, memory paths/rendering, pool promotion, worker launch/IPC and consolidator tool sandboxing, status gauges, and timeline output.
